result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Use a complex gateway only for an explicitly described rule that XOR, OR and AND cannot express. Prefer separate split and join gateways for clarity.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Use gateways to control divergence and convergence, never to represent work. Identify exclusive, inclusive, parallel, event-driven or complex behavior.
Use an exclusive split when exactly one data-based alternative runs. Add supported conditions and at most one default fallback.
Use lanes to partition one process by a stated role, department, system or responsibility; lanes are not separate processes.

result.rule: When the description says that one participant sends an item to another participant and describes the recipient acting on it: Model the participants’ work in their respective processes and connect the communication with a message flow between their pools; keep sequence flows within each participant’s process.

When the description states that one participant sends an item or information to another participant: Label the corresponding BPMN activity from the sender’s perspective and preserve the sending action; do not replace it with the recipient’s receiving perspective.

When the description states that a process participant sends a request or information to an external party and describes that party returning information or otherwise responding: Model the external party as a separate participant pool, keep the sending and receiving work or events in the process participant’s own pool, and represent the exchanges with message flows.

When the description says an external participant sends information to an internal process, which then makes that information available through a user-facing interface: Model the incoming communication to a message-catching event in the internal process, and model making the information available through the interface as a separate internal activity; do not direct the external message to the interface.
